children: , the web domain and hosting provider, rose 12.12% intraday, as of 10:30 a.m. ET, after the Financial Times reported that Gen Digital

, the maker of Norton antivirus software, has made a takeover offer for the company. Talks are at an early stage and may not produce a deal, according to people familiar with the matter, who said the first offer was made in recent weeks. The terms couldn't immediately be established, and both companies declined to comment.

A deal would be transformational for Gen Digital, which has a market value of about $15.7 billion against GoDaddy's roughly $12.2 billion. Formed in 2022 from the merger of NortonLifeLock and Avast, Gen has built itself into a consolidator of consumer security brands such as LifeLock and CCleaner, and it has already moved beyond that core with last year's $1 billion purchase of fintech lender MoneyLion.

GoDaddy would give Gen access to more than 20 million small-business and individual customers and about 81 million web domains, around a fifth of those registered worldwide. GoDaddy reported almost $5 billion in revenue last year, but its shares have fallen 55% from a record high early last year amid concerns that AI website builders could erode its business.

title: GoDaddy Stock Rises After Norton Owner Makes Takeover Approach
